---
title: "A sharper explicit polynomial upper bound for the regular pentagon"
lang: zh-CN
qmd-prover:
  imports:
    - from: reductions.qmd
      use:
        - def-spectral-functional
        - lem-dirichlet-scaling
        - lem-pentagon-polynomial-upper-bound
---

::: {#lem-regular-pentagon-sharper-polynomial-bound .lemma name="An explicit regular-pentagon Rayleigh bound below 18.92" date="2026-09-22" export="lem-regular-pentagon-sharper-polynomial-bound"}
Every regular pentagon $R$ satisfies
$$
F(R)<B_\sharp<\frac{473}{25}=18.92,
$$
where $F$ is the functional of @def-spectral-functional and
$$
\begin{aligned}
z&=\sqrt5,\qquad t=\sqrt{5-2z},\\
M(z)&=2976133761169-1268712226452z,\\
N(z)&=488270310067325-217799942883039z,\\
B_\sharp&=\frac{26}{9}\,t\,\frac{N(z)}{M(z)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
In particular this improves the constant
$B=\frac{66}{7}(5-\sqrt5)\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}$ of
@lem-pentagon-polynomial-upper-bound. The trial value is
$B_\sharp\approx18.91980058994593$; the proof below uses only
exact arithmetic, not this decimal evaluation.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-regular-pentagon-sharper-polynomial-bound" status="verified"}
By @lem-dirichlet-scaling take the inradius of $R$ to be one,
with one outward edge normal equal to $(1,0)$. Its area is $5t$.
Put
$$
r^2=x^2+y^2,\qquad
H_5=x^5-10x^3y^2+5xy^4,
\qquad
p=16-20r^2+5r^4-H_5.
$$
Direct multiplication gives
$$
p=16\prod_{j=0}^4
\left(1-x\cos\frac{2\pi j}{5}-y\sin\frac{2\pi j}{5}\right).
$$
Thus $p$ vanishes on every edge and is positive in the interior.
Choose the integer polynomial
$$
q=-4r^2+6r^6+(1-6r^2)H_5,
\qquad f_0=p,\qquad f_1=pq,
\qquad v=100f_0+f_1.
$$
All these trial functions have zero boundary trace. In particular
$v\in H^1_0(R)$ and $v\not\equiv0$, since $v(0)=1600$.
The polynomials are invariant under rotation through $2\pi/5$.

We give the complete two-dimensional Rayleigh matrices. The five
rotated copies of
$$
T=\{(x,y):0<x<1,\ -tx<y<tx\}
$$
partition $R$ up to null sets. Define the normalized matrices
$$
\mathsf M_{ij}=\frac{297}{20000t}\int_T f_i f_j,
\qquad
\mathsf K_{ij}=\frac{297}{20000t}
                    \int_T\nabla f_i\cdot\nabla f_j,
\qquad i,j\in\{0,1\}.
$$
They are
$$
\mathsf M=\frac1{676715039}
\begin{pmatrix}
676715039&-88189904088+39247847496z\\
-88189904088+39247847496z&
153725250963712-68747756368896z
\end{pmatrix},
$$
$$
\mathsf K=\frac1{780825045}
\begin{pmatrix}
7362064710-1472412942z&-4677664203960+2090632213296z\\
-4677664203960+2090632213296z&
16486562115846400-7373000485496448z
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Every entry can be checked by expanding the displayed polynomials
and using the single monomial rule
$$
\frac1t\int_Tx^m y^n=
\begin{cases}
0,&n\text{ odd},\\
\displaystyle\frac{2(5-2z)^{n/2}}{(n+1)(m+n+2)},&n\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$
Here $m,n$ are nonnegative integers and all subsequent reductions
use only $z^2=5$. As a check on the energy entries, reflection
symmetry gives $\partial_\nu f_j=0$ on both radial sides of $T$,
while $f_i=0$ on its outer side. Hence the same entries are
obtained from $\int_T f_i(-\Delta f_j)$.

For the coefficient vector $c=(100,1)^{\mathsf T}$ the matrices give
$$
c^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M c
=\frac{48M(z)}{676715039},
\qquad
c^{\mathsf T}\mathsf K c
=\frac{32N(z)}{780825045}.
$$
Since $676715039/780825045=13/15$, the Rayleigh principle of
@def-spectral-functional yields
$$
F(R)\leq 5t\,
\frac{c^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Kc}{c^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Mc}
=\frac{26}{9}t\frac{N(z)}{M(z)}=B_\sharp.
$$
The inequality is strict. Otherwise the nonzero polynomial $v$
would be a first eigenfunction and satisfy the polynomial identity
$-\Delta v=\lambda_1(R)v$. Its highest-degree term is
$6r^2H_5^2$, of degree twelve, whereas $\Delta v$ has degree
at most ten and $\lambda_1(R)>0$. This is impossible.

It remains to certify the rational bound on $B_\sharp$.
Use the exact enclosure
$$
\frac{2236067977499}{10^{12}}
<z<\frac{2236067977500}{10^{12}}.
$$
It follows simply by squaring, since
$$
5\cdot10^{24}-2236067977499^2=3531629704999>0,
$$
$$
2236067977500^2-5\cdot10^{24}=940506250000>0.
$$
Both $M(z)$ and $N(z)$ are positive. For an entirely arithmetic
check, their values at the upper endpoint of this enclosure have
numerators
$$
139206978936954359170000,
\qquad 1254832285232464216377500,
$$
respectively, over the positive denominator $10^{12}$.
The coefficients of $z$ in $M,N$ are negative, so these are
strict positive lower bounds for their actual values.

Since all quantities being squared are positive,
$B_\sharp<473/25$ is equivalent to
$$
81\cdot473^2 M(z)^2
-625\cdot26^2(5-2z)N(z)^2>0.
$$
Expansion and $z^2=5$ reduce its left side exactly to
$$
-1902999002282797156863367505533627031
+851047026047032915966440285220798976z.
$$
At the lower endpoint of the enclosure for $z$, this expression
is positive: after multiplication by $10^{12}$ its numerator is
$$
6730508391591047998601635913170241024>0.
$$
Its $z$ coefficient is positive, so the expression is strictly
positive at $z=\sqrt5$. This proves $B_\sharp<473/25$.
Finally the same enclosure gives $B>18.93>18.92$ for the old
constant in @lem-pentagon-polynomial-upper-bound. Explicitly,
$$
B^2=\frac{4356}{49}(250-110z)
>\frac{4356}{49}
\left(250-110\frac{2236067977500}{10^{12}}\right)
>\left(\frac{1893}{100}\right)^2,
$$
where the last comparison is rational arithmetic. Thus the new
constant is strictly smaller than the old one as well.
:::
